whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Order Management Administrator AP exam for?

personas.label: Admins configuring order fulfillment
personas.description: You set up how orders are split, routed and shipped in Salesforce Order Management.

personas.label: Operations managers
personas.description: You own order processing, returns and customer service for orders, and want to understand how the system works.

personas.label: Implementation partners
personas.description: You roll out Order Management alongside B2C or B2B Commerce for clients.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Order Management Administrator AP Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a moderate exam, but the product has its own data model that most admins haven't used. Once you understand how an Order becomes an Order Summary and then Fulfillment Orders, the rest falls into place.
bullets: About 65% to pass, roughly 39 correct answers. Check the official guide for the current figure.
New data model. Order Summary, Fulfillment Order, Return Order, Change Order and their related objects.
Flow-driven processes. Much of the order lifecycle is run by flows, so know which flows do what.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Set up a trial org with Order Management and push a test order all the way through fulfilment, cancellation and return. Before you book, aim for 75% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Order Management Administrator AP Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions are about an order at a certain stage, such as a partial cancellation or a return, and ask which record, flow or setting handles it.
bestWayToPass: Draw the data model: Order, Order Summary, Order Item Summary, Fulfillment Order, Return Order and Change Order.
Follow one order through its life: Placed, routed, fulfilled, invoiced, then cancelled or returned.
Know the role of flows: Many steps, like creating fulfilment orders or handling exceptions, run in flows you can change.
Learn Omnichannel Inventory basics: Locations, location groups, availability and reservations.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you set up and run Salesforce Order Management: the order data model, routing and fulfilment, changes, returns, payments and inventory.

keyConcepts.h2: Order Management Admin AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Order Lifecycle & Order Summary
blocks.body: An order usually arrives from a commerce store or an outside system as an **Order**. Order Management then creates an **Order Summary**, which becomes the main record for everything that happens next. The Order Summary has **Order Item Summaries** for each product and **Order Delivery Group Summaries** for each delivery address and method. The original Order isn't changed after that. All later changes, like cancellations or price adjustments, are recorded against the Order Summary, so you always have both the original order and its current state.

blocks.heading: Fulfillment & Inventory Allocation
blocks.body: To ship an order, Order Management creates **Fulfillment Orders**, each tied to one **Location** such as a warehouse or store. Routing logic, usually in a flow, decides which location fulfils which items, for example the nearest warehouse with stock. One Order Summary can be split across several Fulfillment Orders. Warehouse staff or outside systems update the Fulfillment Order as items are picked, packed and shipped. Once items ship, an **invoice** can be created and payment captured.

blocks.heading: Returns, Refunds & Return Merchandise Authorization
blocks.body: Before shipping, a customer can **cancel** items, which creates a **Change Order** and lowers the amount on the Order Summary. After shipping, a customer **returns** items with a **Return Order** and **Return Order Line Items**. When the return is received, the items are marked as returned and a refund is issued with a **credit memo**. Service agents usually do this from the Order Summary in the console, using built-in actions. The process records why items came back, which helps reporting.

blocks.heading: Pricing, Promotions & Tax
blocks.body: Prices, discounts and taxes come across from the original order and are stored on the Order Summary and its item summaries. When items are cancelled or returned, the system works out how much to refund, including the right share of any order-level discount and tax. Price adjustments, such as a goodwill discount, are recorded as changes so the totals stay correct. Payment records such as **Payment Summaries** track what was authorised, captured and refunded.

blocks.heading: Integration & OCI (Omnichannel Inventory)
blocks.body: **Omnichannel Inventory** tracks stock across locations. **Location groups** let you show availability for a set of locations, such as all warehouses in one country. When an order is placed, stock is **reserved** so it can't be sold twice, and the reservation moves to the fulfilling location when the order is routed. Order Management works closely with B2C and B2B Commerce, and with outside systems like warehouse or ERP systems through APIs and events. Failures in automated steps can be caught and handled as **process exceptions** that agents can review.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Order Management Administrator Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions place you at one point in an order's life. Work out which record changes at that point and which flow or action does the work.

blocks.heading: Order Management Data Model
blocks.body: Order is the original. Order Summary is the living record. Fulfillment Orders ship. Change Orders record cancellations and adjustments. Return Orders handle returns.

blocks.heading: Order Routing & Allocation
blocks.body: Routing decides which location fulfils which items, usually in a flow. One order can be split across locations.

blocks.heading: Order Lifecycle Configuration
blocks.body: Order Summary status shows where the order is. Flows drive most steps, and admins can change them.

blocks.heading: Return & Refund Processing
blocks.body: Cancel before shipping, return after shipping. Refunds use credit memos.

blocks.heading: OM Integration with Commerce
blocks.body: Commerce places the order, Order Management fulfils it, and Omnichannel Inventory keeps stock correct across channels.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Order Management Admin:

sampleQuestions.question: After an order comes in from the online store, which record becomes the main record for tracking its fulfilment, changes and returns?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order Management creates an Order Summary from the Order, and all later activity is recorded against it.
whyWrong: The original Order is kept as it was and isn't updated.
The Account is the customer, not the order.
The cart is gone once the order is placed.

sampleQuestions.question: An order has items shipping from two different warehouses. How is this represented?
options: Two Fulfillment Orders, one for each location
sampleQuestions.explanation: Each Fulfillment Order is tied to one location, so an order split across warehouses gets one per warehouse.
whyWrong: The customer is the same.
Return Orders are for returns.
There is one Order Summary per order.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer cancels one item before it has shipped. What does Order Management create?
options: A Change Order that reduces the Order Summary
sampleQuestions.explanation: Cancellations before shipping are recorded as Change Orders, which adjust the Order Summary totals.
whyWrong: A new Order isn't needed.
A Case may be logged, but it doesn't change the order.
Return Orders are for items that have already shipped.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer wants to send back a shipped item for a refund. What should the agent use?
options: A Return Order with Return Order Line Items
A Change Order to cancel the item
sampleQuestions.explanation: Shipped items are returned through a Return Order. When received, the refund is processed.
whyWrong: Deleting records loses history and breaks totals.
The original Order should not be changed.
Cancellation is for items that haven't shipped yet.

sampleQuestions.question: The business wants orders sent to the warehouse closest to the customer that has stock. Where is this logic usually set up?
options: In the routing flow that creates Fulfillment Orders
sampleQuestions.explanation: Routing is usually handled by a flow that picks locations and creates Fulfillment Orders. Admins can change its logic.
whyWrong: Product descriptions can't route orders.
Reports show data but don't act on it.
Page layouts don't route orders.

sampleQuestions.question: The online store must show stock available across all warehouses in Germany. What should be configured?
options: A separate store for each warehouse
A custom field on each product
A daily email from each warehouse
A location group in Omnichannel Inventory containing the German warehouses
sampleQuestions.explanation: Location groups combine availability for several locations, which the store can then show.
whyWrong: Separate stores don't combine stock.
A custom field must be updated by hand and goes out of date.
Emails don't feed the store.

sampleQuestions.question: Why does Order Management reserve stock when an order is placed?
options: So the same item isn't sold twice before it ships
To hide the product from search
sampleQuestions.explanation: A reservation holds the stock for that order until it is fulfilled, so other buyers can't buy it.
whyWrong: Reservations don't change prices.
Invoices come after shipping.
Search visibility isn't affected.

sampleQuestions.question: A step in an order flow fails because a payment service didn't respond. How can agents find and fix these orders?
options: Review the process exceptions created for the failures
sampleQuestions.explanation: Process exceptions record failures in automated steps so agents can see and resolve them.
whyWrong: Waiting for complaints harms customers.
Emails aren't a reliable list of failures.
Deleting orders loses sales.

sampleQuestions.question: A service agent gives a customer a goodwill discount on an order that has already been placed. How should it be recorded?
options: By editing the original Order's total
As a price adjustment recorded against the Order Summary
sampleQuestions.explanation: Adjustments are recorded as changes on the Order Summary, so totals and refunds stay correct.
whyWrong: A note doesn't change the amount owed.
The original Order should stay unchanged.
Deleting items misstates what the customer bought.

sampleQuestions.question: An order had a 10% order-level discount. The customer returns one of three items. What should the refund include?
options: The item's price less its share of the discount, plus its share of tax
The full item price with no discount
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order Management spreads order-level discounts and tax across items, so the refund reflects what was actually paid for that item.
whyWrong: Only the returned item is refunded.
Refunding the full price ignores the discount the customer received.
Discounted orders can still be refunded.

sampleQuestions.question: When can payment usually be captured for items in an order?
options: When the items ship and an invoice is created
sampleQuestions.explanation: Capturing payment is usually tied to shipping, with an invoice created for what has shipped.
whyWrong: Signing up has no payment attached.
A cart isn't an order yet.
Returns lead to refunds, not captures.

sampleQuestions.question: Which record tracks one product line in an Order Summary, including how many were ordered, cancelled and returned?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Each Order Item Summary holds the quantities for one product line, including changes over time.
whyWrong: A Fulfillment Order covers shipping from one location.
A Location is a warehouse or store.
A Payment Summary tracks payments.

sampleQuestions.question: Customers can choose different delivery addresses for different items in one order. Which record groups items by delivery address and method?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order Delivery Group Summaries group items by where and how they are delivered.
whyWrong: Return Orders are for returns.
Change Orders record changes.
Credit memos record refunds.

sampleQuestions.question: A warehouse system needs to tell Salesforce when a Fulfillment Order ships. What is the best approach?
options: Update the Fulfillment Order through the API or an integration
sampleQuestions.explanation: Outside systems update the Fulfillment Order status through APIs, which moves the order forward automatically.
whyWrong: A new Order would duplicate the sale.
The Account doesn't track shipping.
Email needs someone to update the record by hand.

sampleQuestions.question: Where do service agents usually handle cancellations and returns?
options: From the Order Summary in the console, using the built-in actions
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Order Management console gives agents actions like Cancel Item and Return Item on the Order Summary.
whyWrong: The Developer Console is for code.
Setup is for admins, not daily order work.
Data Loader is for bulk data, not single orders.
